title: No faction in the kingdom of God
source_text: Ἑξῆς δὲ τούτοις φησί· καὶ μὴν ὅ γε φάσκων ἕνα εἰρῆσθαι κύριον, περὶ θεοῦ λέγων. ἀσεβεῖ διαιρῶν τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ βασιλείαν καὶ στασιάζων. ὡς οὔσης αἱρέσεως καὶ ὄντος τινὸς ἑτέρου ἀντιστασιώτου αὐτῷ. χώραν δ᾿ εἶχεν αὐτῷ ταῦτα, εἰ γραμμικαῖς ἀποδείξεσι παρίστη τοὺς ὑπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν προσκυνουμένους ὡς θεοὺς θεοὺς εἶναι, καὶ τοὺς περὶ τὰ ἀγάλματα καὶ τοὺς νεὼς καὶ τοὺς βωμοὺς νομιζομένους τυγχάνειν παρίστη μὴ ὄντας φαύλους τινὰς δαίμονας. ἀλλὰ καὶ τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ βασιλείαν παρ᾿ ἡμῖν συνεχῶς λεγομένην καὶ γεγραμμένην ἡμεῖς μὲν καὶ νοεῖν εὐχόμεθα καὶ τοιοῦτοι γίνεσθαι, ἵν᾿ ὑπὸ θεοῦ μόνου βασιλευώμεθα, καὶ γένηται καὶ ἡμῶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ. ἐκεῖνος δὲ, πολλοὺς ἡμᾶς διδάσκων σέβειν θεοὺς. θεῶν μᾶλλον ὤφειλεν, εἰ τὰ ἀκόλουθα ἑαυτῷ σκοπεῖ. λέγειν βασιλείαν ἤπερ θεοῦ. οὔτ᾿ οὖν αἱρέσεις παρὰ θεῷ οὔτ᾿ ἐστί τις θεὸς ἀντιστασιώτης αὐτῷ, κἂν οἷον Γίγαντές τινες ἢ Τιτᾶνες διὰ τὴν ἰδίαν φαυλότητα θεομαχεῖν θέλωσι μετὰ Κέλσου καὶ τῶν ἀραμένων πόλεμον πρὸς τὸν διὰ μυρίων παραστήσαντα τὰ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν τὸν ἐπὶ σωτηρίᾳ τοῦ γένους ἡμῶν παντὶ τῷ κόσμῳ ἀθρόως ἑαυτὸν ὄντα λόγον, ὡς ἕκαστος χωρεῖ, ἐπιδεδωκότα.
pass_a_gloss: Next to these he says: 'and indeed the one asserting (φάσκων) that one Lord (ἕνα κύριον) has been spoken of, speaking about God, is impious (ἀσεβεῖ), dividing (διαιρῶν) the kingdom (βασιλεία) of God and making faction (στασιάζων), as though there were a party/faction (αἵρεσις) and some other rival-in-faction (ἀντιστασιώτης) to Him.' These would have had a place (χώραν εἶχεν) for him if by geometrical demonstrations (γραμμικαῖς ἀποδείξεσι) he established that those worshipped (προσκυνουμένους) by the nations (ἔθνη) as gods are gods, and established that those thought to be present (τυγχάνειν) about the statues (ἀγάλματα) and the temples (νεώς) and the altars (βωμούς) are not some wicked daemons/demons (φαύλους δαίμονας). But also the kingdom of God continually spoken and written among us, we pray (εὐχόμεθα) both to understand (νοεῖν) and to become such that we may be ruled as by a king (βασιλευώμεθα) by God alone, and the kingdom of God may come to be ours also. But he, teaching us to revere (σέβειν) many gods, ought rather, if he considers the consequences (τὰ ἀκόλουθα) for himself, to say a kingdom of gods than of God. Neither then are there factions with God nor is there some god rival-in-faction to Him, even if, like some Giants or Titans, through their own wickedness (φαυλότης) they wish to fight God (θεομαχεῖν) with Celsus and those who have raised war (ἀραμένων πόλεμον) against the One who through countless [proofs] (διὰ μυρίων) established the things about Jesus, and against Him Himself who, for the salvation (σωτηρία) of our race (γένος), gave Himself (ἑαυτὸν ἐπιδεδωκότα), being the Word, to the whole world all at once (ἀθρόως), as each has room/capacity (χωρεῖ).
pass_b_english: Next after this he says: “And yet the one who, speaking about God, asserts that one Lord is meant is impious, because he divides the kingdom of God and creates faction, as though there were a party, and some other rival opposed to Him.”

This would have had some force for him if he had proved by geometrical demonstrations that those whom the nations worship as gods really are gods, and had shown that those who are believed to dwell about statues and temples and altars are not some wicked demons. But as for the kingdom of God, which is constantly spoken of and written about among us, we pray both to understand it and to become such that we may be ruled by God alone, and that the kingdom of God may become ours also. He, on the other hand, who teaches us to revere many gods, ought, if he looks at what follows from his own position, to speak of a kingdom of gods rather than of God.

So there are no factions with God, nor is there any god who is His rival, even if some, like Giants or Titans, wish through their own wickedness to fight against God, together with Celsus and those who have taken up war against Him who in countless ways established what concerns Jesus, and against Jesus Himself, who for the salvation of our race gave Himself, being the Word, to the whole world at once, as each is able to receive Him.

choices.choice: Celsus’s ‘one Lord’ refers back to the saying about not serving two masters discussed in 8.2 (Matthew 6:24); his words do not quote a verse and the allusion is indirect, so no inline citation is given inside his words. ‘Speaking about God, asserts that one Lord is meant’ renders φάσκων ἕνα εἰρῆσθαι κύριον, περὶ θεοῦ λέγων. αἵρεσις is rendered ‘party’ (faction), not ‘heresy’; ἀντιστασιώτης ‘rival’. δαίμονας is rendered ‘demons’ in Origen’s voice. ‘Dwell about’ renders νομιζομένους τυγχάνειν περὶ (believed to be present about). ‘May be ruled by God alone ... the kingdom of God may become ours’ is a possible echo of Matthew 6:10 or Luke 17:21; not cited because uncertain. ‘Him who in countless ways established what concerns Jesus’ is God (διὰ μυρίων, ‘through countless [means]’; τὰ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ‘the things concerning Jesus’). ‘Jesus Himself’ makes explicit the referent of αὐτὸν. ‘Receive Him’ renders χωρεῖ (has room for); ‘Him’ is supplied for English.
Celsus's quote: removed inner quotation marks around 'one Lord' (no verse is quoted) and set περὶ θεοῦ λέγων in its place: 'the one who, speaking about God, asserts that one Lord is meant'

'stirs up faction, as though there were rival parties and some other who opposes Him in faction' -> 'creates faction, as though there were a party, and some other rival opposed to Him' (αἱρέσεως is singular)
'haunt statues' -> 'dwell about statues' (τυγχάνειν περὶ; removed added colouring)
'any god who opposes Him in faction' -> 'any god who is His rival'
'by countless proofs established the truth about Jesus' -> 'in countless ways established what concerns Jesus' (no supplied 'proofs' or 'truth')
